# AQ host catalog 2.6.0

The delivery lineage of catalog 2.3.0, so that a delivery playbook can judge a
result that changed nothing: did the agent's conclusion show that the task's
acceptance criteria are met without a change? Code provides the facts and the
judgment; the playbook decides whether to complete the task or send it back.

## Changed

- `work.read` 2.6.0: two more facts, always present.
  - `acceptance_criteria`: the task's acceptance criteria, a string of at most
    8192 bytes (the graph's bound), `""` when the task has none. It is not
    part of `description`.
  - `conclusion`: the conclusion the agent reported with the task's latest
    result, a string of at most 512 bytes (the result report's bound), `""`
    when the task has no result yet.

  Both fit a `judgment.assess` context item (`text`, at most 8192 bytes). A
  2.3.0 answer no longer fits, so an artifact sealed on 2.3.0 keeps its 2.3.0
  `work.read`; the capability stays `work.read`.

Every other contract of 2.3.0, and every event, is byte-identical.
`judgment.assess` is unchanged: its `rationale` (at most 4096 bytes) does not
fit `work.return`'s `detail` (at most 1024 bytes), so a playbook that sends a
task back gives its own sentence as the detail.

## Files

`registry.json`, `manifest.json`, `fixtures.json` and `notes.json` are
generated by `crates/aq-playbooks-cli/tests/catalog_v2_6_contract.rs` and
pinned by `generated_catalog_files_are_pinned`. Regenerate from the workspace
root with `cargo test -p aq-playbooks-cli --test catalog_v2_6_contract
write_catalog_v2_6 -- --ignored`. The same file seals a playbook that judges an
unchanged result and runs its two cases
(`a_delivery_playbook_can_judge_an_unchanged_result`).
